sessions.title: Setup and SKU list
sessions.goal: Set up schema, migrate and seed, list SKUs via API and table.

criteria.check: GET /api/skus returns 200 with a JSON array of SKU with length 8
sc-skus-list renders exactly 8 elements with data-testid=sku-row

cuts.hint: Put every SKU the store holds into `body` and set `status` to 200
Fetch GET /api/skus and write the parsed array into `items`, then render one row per SKU

sessions.title: Reorder suggestions
sessions.goal: Compute qty_to_order server-side and show only positive rows.

criteria.check: GET /api/reorder-suggestions returns 200 with Suggestion[] where for every item qty_to_order == max(0, reorder_point - on_hand)
sc-suggestions renders one data-testid=suggestion-row per item where qty_to_order > 0, and none where qty_to_order == 0
Each rendered suggestion row shows its qty_to_order in a cell with data-testid=qty-to-order

cuts.hint: Build `body` as an array of { sku_id, name, on_hand, reorder_point, qty_to_order } where qty_to_order is max(0, reorder_point - on_hand), and set `status` to 200
Fetch GET /api/reorder-suggestions and write the parsed array into `suggestions`
Write into `visible` only the suggestions whose qty_to_order is greater than 0

sessions.title: Commit a suggested order
sessions.goal: Select suggestions, POST them to create a purchase order in one transaction, and show a confirmation.

criteria.check: POST /api/purchase-orders with lines [{sku_id, qty}] returns 200 with JSON { id: number, itemsCount: number, totalQty: number }
sc-suggestions renders a button with data-testid=po-submit whose text includes '(2)' after two rows are checked
After selecting rows and clicking Create Purchase Order, the app navigates to /purchase-orders/created?items=<n>&total=<m>
sc-po-created renders the two numbers from the URL (data-testid=po-created-items and data-testid=po-created-total)

cuts.hint: When a row’s checkbox is toggled, add or remove that sku_id in `selected` and leave all other ids unchanged

Build a JSON body from the current `selected` using each line’s qty_to_order, POST it to /api/purchase-orders, and set `nav` to /purchase-orders/created?items={itemsCount}&total={totalQty} when it succeeds

In one transaction, insert a new PurchaseOrder with a fixed created_label (e.g. 'manual'), insert one PurchaseOrderItem per line, then set `body` to { id, itemsCount: number of lines, totalQty: sum of qty } and `status` to 200
Read the items and total numbers from the page URL and write { itemsCount, totalQty } into `summary`

sessions.title: Purchase order history and detail
sessions.goal: List prior POs with totals and show a detail page of its lines.

criteria.check: GET /api/purchase-orders returns 200 with an array of { id, itemsCount, totalQty }
sc-po-history renders one data-testid=po-row per order and shows both itemsCount and totalQty on each row
GET /api/purchase-orders/:id returns 200 with { id, lines: [{ sku_id, name, qty }], itemsCount, totalQty }
sc-po-detail renders one data-testid=po-line per line, each showing a SKU name and qty

cuts.hint: Fetch GET /api/purchase-orders and write the parsed array into `orders`
Query purchase orders with an aggregate to produce { id, itemsCount, totalQty } for each order, write the array into `body`, and set `status` to 200
Query a single purchase order’s lines joined to SKU names, compute itemsCount and totalQty, write { id, lines, itemsCount, totalQty } into `body`, and set `status` to 200
Fetch GET /api/purchase-orders/:id for the current id and write the parsed object into `po`
